cleanIntro:
The Centurion 11 is a 1911-pattern .45 ACP pistol: single action, a 5-inch barrel held by a swinging link, a barrel bushing at the muzzle, and a thumb safety and a grip safety. The strip starts at the muzzle. The recoil spring plug is pressed in and the bushing turned off it, then the slide stop comes out and the slide runs forward off the frame. The spring behind the plug is compressed, and Century Arms repeats the same eye-protection warning through the strip and again at assembly, so put glasses on before you start.

Century Arms asks for a clean after every day of shooting. This is the Centurion 11 book; it does not mention the Centurion 11 TAC's rail or optic cut.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Press the magazine release, on the left side of the frame behind the trigger guard, and take the magazine out of the grip.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the slide moves. Work the slide with a loaded magazine still in and it feeds the next round into the chamber you are about to check.
steps.quote: With the firearm pointed in a safe direction and finger off the trigger, press the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Removing the Magazine, printed p.19

steps.title: Slide back and locked open
steps.action: Still pointed safely, finger still off the trigger, put the thumb safety down, pull the slide all the way to the rear, and push up on the slide stop so the slide stays open.
steps.prose: The safety has to be down for this: in the safe position it sits up in a recess in the slide. The slide is held when it stays back with your hand off it. If it creeps forward, the slide stop did not reach its notch; pull back fully and push up again.
steps.quote: While maintaining a safe direction with your finger off the trigger, pull the slide to the rear and lock back by using upward pressure on the slide stop.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Removing the Magazine, printed p.19

steps.title: Look into the chamber and feel it
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the chamber and put a fingertip in it. Look down the empty magazine well as well. Do not go on until you have done both.
steps.prose: Century Arms asks for a visual and a physical check because a glance into a dark chamber can miss a case.
steps.quote: Visually and physically inspect the chamber to ensure the pistol is free of ammunition
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Removing the Magazine, printed p.19
steps.warn: Never assume a gun is unloaded - even if you were the last person to use it.

steps.title: Plug pressed in, bushing a quarter turn clockwise
steps.action: Let the slide forward on the empty chamber. Press the recoil spring plug in, under the barrel at the muzzle, and turn the barrel bushing 90 degrees clockwise to uncover the plug. Keep your thumb over the plug as the bushing clears it.
steps.prose: The bushing is the only thing holding the plug in, and the recoil spring is compressed behind it. Let the plug come out under your thumb, never on its own, and keep it pointed away from your face.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring plug in and rotate the barrel bushing 90 ° clockwise.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.20
steps.warn: Wear eye protection to avoid injury from flying springs or recoil spring plug.

steps.title: Plug out, and the spring if it comes easily
steps.action: Take the recoil spring plug out. If the recoil spring comes out easily, take it now. If it does not, leave it where it is.
steps.prose: Do not fight the spring here. Left in, it comes out with the guide rod once the slide is off.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring plug. If the recoil spring is easly removed, do so at this time. If not, leave installed.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.20

steps.title: Bushing back, then on past, and out
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing counterclockwise 90 degrees, back to where it started, and then about 45 degrees further, until it can be pulled out of the slide.
steps.prose: The extra 45 degrees is what frees it. Stop at the starting position and the bushing will feel stuck; it is still locked in the slide.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel bushing back counter clockwise 90° and then 45° further until it can be removed.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.21

steps.title: Half-moon notch lined up, slide stop out
steps.action: Push the slide slowly rearward until the half-moon notch in its lower edge lines up with the rear of the slide stop. Press the stop from the right side of the frame and pull it out from the left.
steps.prose: The stop leaves only at that notch. If pressing from the right moves nothing, the notch is not lined up; move the slide a little rather than pushing harder.
steps.quote: Remove the slide stop by slowly pushing the slide rearward until the half moon detent notch lines up with the rear of the stop and then press the stop from the right side and pull out from the left.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.21

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Push or pull the slide slowly forward until it comes off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: With the slide stop out, nothing else keeps the slide on its rails, so hold it all the way and keep the muzzle end level.
steps.quote: Remove the slide by slowly pushing/pulling it forward off the frame.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.21

steps.title: Guide rod and spring out
steps.action: Take the recoil spring guide rod out of the slide, and the recoil spring with it if you left it in.
steps.prose: Note which way the guide rod faces before it comes out, so it goes back the same way.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring guide rod, and recoil spring if it is still installed.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.21

steps.title: Barrel unlocked and out
steps.action: Lift the barrel to unlock it from the slide, then take it out of the slide.
steps.prose: It will not slide out until it is lifted: the lugs on top of the barrel have to leave the slide first.
steps.quote: Lift to unlock and then remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Disassembly, printed p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the receiver, the slide, the barrel, the barrel bushing, the guide rod, the recoil spring plug, the recoil spring, the slide stop and the magazine. That is every part Century Arms takes off for cleaning.
steps.prose: Count nine before you open the solvent. The firing pin, the extractor, the grip safety and everything inside the frame stay where they are.
steps.quote: 1-RECEIVER ASSEMBLY 2-SLIDE ASSEMBLY 3-BARREL 4-BARREL BUSHING 5-GUIDE ROD 6-RECOIL SPRING PLUG 7-RECOIL SPRING 8-SLIDE STOP 9-MAGAZINE ASSEMBLY
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Parts to Disassemble for Cleaning, printed p.22

steps.title: Bore from the breech end
steps.action: Use a pistol cleaning rod with a tip and a patch of the right caliber that fits the bore snugly. Put the rod and patch in at the breech end of the barrel and run it back and forth several times.
steps.prose: With the barrel out of the slide there is no reason to work from the muzzle: the breech end is open and the crown stays untouched.
steps.quote: Insert the rod and patch into the barrel at the breech end and run it back and forth several times.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.23

steps.title: Bore dry, then a lightly oiled patch
steps.action: When the fouling is gone, wipe the chamber and bore dry. Then run a slightly oiled patch through the bore to preserve it, with a fine, light gun oil. Look through the barrel and chamber to be sure no patch is left inside.
steps.prose: A patch left in the barrel is an obstruction. So is too much oil: the book warns that even excess lubricating oil in the bore can raise pressure, so the patch is slightly oiled and no more.
steps.quote: When the bore is dry, pass a slightly oiled patch through it for preservation. A fine, light gun oil is recommended.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.24

steps.title: Slide and action brushed, moving parts oiled
steps.action: Use a small brush or a rag to take dirt and other foreign matter off the slide and the other parts of the action. Then lightly lubricate all the moving parts with a high-quality, light gun oil.
steps.prose: Lightly is the instruction. On the parts in front of you, the moving surfaces are the slide and frame rails, the barrel and its link, the bushing, and the recoil spring and its guide.
steps.quote: Use a small brush or rag to remove dirt or other foreign matter from the slide and other parts of the action. Lightly lubricate all moving parts with a high-quality, light gun oil.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.24

steps.title: Outside metal wiped, finger marks off
steps.action: Wipe all the exposed metal with a lightly oiled cloth until every finger mark is gone. Do it again any time the pistol has been out in the weather or handled.
steps.prose: Finger marks are the point of this step: the book says they give moisture somewhere to collect.
steps.quote: Finger marks provide a place where moisture can accumulate.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.24

steps.title: Plastic grips: oil or wax, not both
steps.action: Wipe the plastic grips with a quality, lightweight gun oil, or polish them with a quality furniture wax. Use one or the other.
steps.prose: The book's bracket is the instruction: but not both.
steps.quote: The plastic grips can also be wiped with a quality, lightweight gun oil or polished with any quality furniture wax (but not both).
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL — CENTURION 11 — undated — no edition, revision code or print date is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.24

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean in the Centurion 11 book. It publishes one disassembly (printed pp.20-21) and shows the nine assemblies that leaves you with as the parts to disassemble for cleaning (printed p.22). The firing pin, extractor, mainspring housing, sear and grip safety appear only in the part list (printed p.28 on) and the exploded view, with no procedure, and the magazine is kept whole. Its alterations warning says to have a qualified gunsmith work on the gun, or at least check any work a gunsmith did not do.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Snug patch on a pistol rod, in at the breech end, back and forth several times
Chamber and bore wiped dry once all the fouling is out
One slightly oiled patch through the dry bore, with a fine, light gun oil
Look through the barrel and chamber: no patch left inside
⛔ No oil standing in the bore when the pistol is fired

cleaning.name: SLIDE & ACTION
tasks: Dirt and foreign matter off the slide and the other action parts with a small brush or rag
All moving parts lightly lubricated with a high-quality, light gun oil
⛔ Never spray or put lubricant on ammunition

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & GRIPS
tasks: All exposed metal wiped with a lightly oiled cloth, every finger mark off
A light film of oil on the metal after weather or handling
Plastic grips: lightweight gun oil or furniture wax, not both

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Cleaned and lightly lubricated before it goes away, with a light coat of good gun oil on exposed surfaces and the excess removed
Checked unloaded before storing, and before any locking device goes on
Coming out of storage: rod and patch through the bore, dry and free of obstructions, before firing

reassembly: Eye protection stays on: the spring and plug go back under pressure.
Slide onto the frame. Hold it there: nothing else keeps it on until the slide stop is in.
Guide rod back in under the barrel, the same way it came out.
Barrel bushing in at the muzzle, turned clockwise all the way.
Recoil spring in at the front of the slide, under the barrel.
With the pistol pointed in a safe direction, push the recoil spring plug in.
Turn the barrel bushing counterclockwise to lock it over the plug.
Pull the slide back a little, put the slide stop through the frame and the hole in the barrel link, and snap it into place.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber proven empty, muzzle safe, finger off the trigger throughout. Pull the slide fully back and let it go forward: it should run smoothly and close completely. Pull it back again and push up on the slide stop: it should stay locked open with your hand off it. Close it. With the hammer cocked, push the thumb safety up into its recess in the slide and back down; it should stop in both positions. Century Arms notes that the safety cannot go up with the hammer down. Check that the bushing holds the plug and that the slide stop is fully seated. If anything binds or does not work, stop and take the pistol to a qualified gunsmith or Century Arms.
